chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 312: Madman – Li Huowang’s Lowest Point
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang hits rock bottom. After slaughtering Bai Lingmiao’s family, he wanders in the rain, confronts his hallucinations, and ends up a homeless man eating from trash—accepting the label “madman.”
og_title: Madman – Chapter 312 of Dao Gui Yi Xian
og_description: Li Huowang’s last shred of hope is gone. He tries to die, fails, and finds himself a scavenger on the street, laughing as a child throws a stone at him.
twitter_title: The Chapter Where Li Huowang Breaks
twitter_description: After killing Bai Lingmiao’s clan, Li Huowang wanders in the rain, nearly suicides, and ends up eating from a trash can. He accepts being called a madman.

lore_anchors.definition: A rare, innate constitution that makes a person able to shape reality through belief. In the Dao-Twisted World, being a Heart-Element is less a power and more a curse: every thought can become real, including the worst ones.
A military-grade blade saturated with killing intent (sha qi). It corrupts ordinary wielders with bloodlust but can be held safely by those with special constitutions like Li Huowang’s.
One of Li Huowang’s persistent hallucinations. He represents cynical trickery and schadenfreude, often mocking the protagonist’s choices with the glee of a Zuowandao liar.
Another hallucination of Li Huowang’s, representing hollow piety and guilt. He offers shallow Buddhist comfort that rings false even inside Li Huowang’s own head.
A hallucination of a female soldier, clad in armor, who shows silent contempt for Li Huowang’s weakness; she embodies martial disdain and unreachable strength.
A mute hallucination who only watches Li Huowang with concern; his silence holds a heavy, sorrowful weight that words cannot express.
The Bai family’s ancestral village; the site of a massacre in the previous chapter where Li Huowang, possessed by Danyangzi, slaughtered Bai Lingmiao’s entire clan.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can’t Li Huowang cut his hallucinations with the sword?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because they are not separate beings—they are projections of his own fractured mind. He cannot injure them any more than he can injure his own shadow.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the “modern world” scene really real?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the novel’s structure, the “real world” (hospital, Yang Na, the bridge underpass) is a hallucination layer. But the horror is that Li Huowang can never confirm which layer is real; both cause him equal pain.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang laugh at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He has exhausted all resistance. The label “madman” is no longer an insult—it is the only identity that fits. The laugh is the sound of surrender.
